meeting.title: Modal x Quarry — weekly implementation sync
meeting.summary: Weekly sync on the Modal onboarding. Reviewed warehouse connectivity blockers, agreed next steps on the usage events model, IP allowlisting, and pilot dashboard sign-off.
action_items: Theo to open PR with incremental model config for usage events by June 18
Jonas to add Quarry static IPs to warehouse network policy by June 17
Priya to circulate pilot dashboard list for guild sign-off by June 19
key_decisions: Usage events model will be incremental, partitioned by event date
meeting.notes: Modal team is moving fast; main risk is the network policy change sitting in their infra queue.

transcript.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
transcript.text: Morning everyone, let's run through the board. Priya, anything urgent before we start?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raman
transcript.text: Nothing urgent. The team is happy with the explore experience so far, we just need the usage events data in.

transcript.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
transcript.text: Great. Theo, where are we on the usage events model?

transcript.speaker: Theo Okonkwo
transcript.text: I looked at the volumes — about forty million rows a day — so a full refresh is off the table. It needs to be incremental, partitioned by event date.

transcript.speaker: Jonas Beck
transcript.text: That matches what we do elsewhere in the project. Do you want to write that config or should we?

transcript.speaker: Theo Okonkwo
transcript.text: I'll take it. I'll draft the incremental model config for the usage events table and have it in a PR by Thursday the 18th.

transcript.speaker: Jonas Beck
transcript.text: Perfect, I'll review it same day.

transcript.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
transcript.text: Next blocker: the connection from our cloud is still being refused by your warehouse. Jonas, that's the network policy, right?

transcript.speaker: Jonas Beck
transcript.text: Yes, it's on me. I'll add the Quarry static IPs to our warehouse network policy — I can get that done by end of day Wednesday, June 17th.

transcript.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
transcript.text: That unblocks the scheduled refreshes, thank you. Priya, last one is pilot scope.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raman
transcript.text: Right. I have a shortlist of six dashboards but I want the analytics guild to agree on which four make the pilot. I'll circulate the pilot dashboard list to the analytics guild and get sign-off by Friday the 19th.

transcript.speaker: Theo Okonkwo
transcript.text: Six to four sounds right for a pilot.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raman
transcript.text: One more thing — at some point we should think about row-level security for the sales team, but that's not a today problem.

transcript.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
transcript.text: Agreed, let's park row-level security until after the pilot. Anything else?

transcript.speaker: Jonas Beck
transcript.text: Nope, all clear on our side.

transcript.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
transcript.text: Great, short and sharp. Talk next Monday.

meeting.title: Function Health security review — working session
meeting.summary: Working session to unstick the Function Health security review (health-data infosec). Agreed the questionnaire handoff, the pen test evidence, and the service account provisioning sequence.
action_items: Ines to return completed SIG Lite questionnaire by June 5
Freya to upload pen test summary to the portal by June 8
Oliver to provision read-only Snowflake service account by June 10
key_decisions: Service account provisioning proceeds immediately after security sign-off, no separate change board review
meeting.notes: The health-data security review has been the blocking chain for three weeks; this session set concrete dates on each link.

transcript.speaker: Ines Ferreira
transcript.text: Thanks for making time, both. The goal today is to get the security review moving again — it's been the blocker for three weeks.

transcript.speaker: Freya Dunn
transcript.text: Honest answer from our side: the review is stuck because we're missing two inputs — your completed SIG Lite questionnaire and evidence from a recent penetration test. Handling patient lab results, our infosec team can't wave either through.

transcript.speaker: Ines Ferreira
transcript.text: The questionnaire is ninety percent done, our security lead has the last section. I'll send the completed SIG Lite questionnaire back to Freya by June 5th.

transcript.speaker: Freya Dunn
transcript.text: Friday works. If I have it Friday, I can start the internal review the following week.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: And the pen test — we have the Q1 report from our external testers. Do you need the full report or a summary?

transcript.speaker: Freya Dunn
transcript.text: A summary with scope and findings severity is enough. Actually, easier if it lives with the rest of the evidence — I'll get the pen test summary uploaded to your portal by Monday, June 8th, once Sam shares it.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: I'll email it to you right after this call, it's ready to go.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Hartley
transcript.text: Then the last link in the chain is me. The warehouse team won't create the service account until security signs off — and with PHI in the schema they're strict about it.

transcript.speaker: Ines Ferreira
transcript.text: Can we pre-agree the shape so it's a same-day job once you get the green light?

transcript.speaker: Oliver Hartley
transcript.text: Yes — read-only, scoped to the ANALYTICS schema, key-pair auth. I'll provision the read-only Snowflake service account as soon as security signs off — targeting Wednesday, June 10th.

transcript.speaker: Freya Dunn
transcript.text: That's realistic if the questionnaire lands Friday.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Do we need your change advisory board for the account creation? That added two weeks last time at another customer.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Hartley
transcript.text: No — we agreed internally last month that read-only analytics accounts skip the change board. It goes straight through.

transcript.speaker: Ines Ferreira
transcript.text: Excellent. So: questionnaire Friday the 5th, pen test summary Monday the 8th, service account Wednesday the 10th. That's the chain unblocked.

transcript.speaker: Freya Dunn
transcript.text: Agreed. Nice to have dates on it at last.

transcript.speaker: Ines Ferreira
transcript.text: Thanks all — I'll recap in the portal after this.

meeting.title: Ashby embedded analytics — weekly sync
meeting.summary: Weekly sync on the Ashby embedded analytics rollout. Agreed sandbox setup with signed JWT auth, the customer_id claim work on Ashby's side, and a write-up of the row-level filtering approach.
action_items: Theo to set up embed sandbox with signed JWT auth and share credentials by June 24
Ruben to expose customer_id claim in session token on staging by June 26
Maya to send row-level filtering write-up for multi-tenant embeds by June 25
key_decisions: Embeds authenticate via signed JWTs minted by Ashby's backend, not shared links
meeting.notes: Ashby wants hiring dashboards inside their recruiting product for their own customers — tenant isolation is the make-or-break requirement.

transcript.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
transcript.text: Hi both — today is all embedded analytics. Elise, want to restate the goal so we're aligned?

transcript.speaker: Elise Vandamme
transcript.text: Sure. We want each of our recruiting customers to see their own dashboards inside our product — their pipeline, their time-to-hire, nobody else's. Tenant isolation is non-negotiable.

transcript.speaker: Theo Okonkwo
transcript.text: Understood. The right pattern here is signed JWTs: your backend mints a short-lived token per user, the token carries the tenant identity, and the embed respects it.

transcript.speaker: Ruben De Smet
transcript.text: That works for us — we already issue session tokens, we'd just extend the claims.

transcript.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
transcript.text: Good. Let's make it concrete. Theo, can you stand up a sandbox they can develop against?

transcript.speaker: Theo Okonkwo
transcript.text: Yes — I'll set up the embed sandbox with signed JWT auth and share credentials by Wednesday, June 24th.

transcript.speaker: Ruben De Smet
transcript.text: Then the ball is with me. I'll expose the customer_id claim in our session token — deployed to staging by Friday, June 26th.

transcript.speaker: Elise Vandamme
transcript.text: One question — how does the customer_id claim actually filter the data? Is that per dashboard or global?

transcript.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
transcript.text: Global, enforced at the semantic layer, so a dashboard can't accidentally leak across tenants. I'll write up the row-level filtering approach for multi-tenant embeds and send it over by Thursday the 25th.

transcript.speaker: Elise Vandamme
transcript.text: Great, I'd like our security folks to read that before we go further.

transcript.speaker: Theo Okonkwo
transcript.text: Sensible. The write-up plus the sandbox should give them everything they need to poke at it.

transcript.speaker: Ruben De Smet
transcript.text: It might be worth load-testing the embeds eventually, but let's see it working first.

transcript.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
transcript.text: Agreed — load testing is a later conversation. So: sandbox Wednesday, write-up Thursday, staging claim Friday. Reconvene next Monday?

transcript.speaker: Elise Vandamme
transcript.text: Works for us. Thanks both.

meeting.title: Function Health implementation catch-up
meeting.summary: Catch-up on the stalled Function Health implementation. The security review that has been blocking everything is nearly complete: Nadia is waiting on one approval from their platform lead and expects to close it out early next week. Oliver will provision the Snowflake service account (read-only on ANALYTICS, no raw layer) the same day security signs off, which unblocks the repo connection.
action_items: Nadia to close out the security review early next week (waiting on platform lead approval)
Oliver to provision the Snowflake service account (read-only, ANALYTICS schema) the same day security signs off
key_decisions: Service account scope confirmed as read-only on the ANALYTICS schema only — no access to the raw layer holding identifiable lab results
meeting.notes: The infosec and HIPAA questionnaire has been the bottleneck for three weeks. Nadia has the remaining answers drafted and is waiting on one internal approval.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Thanks for making time. I know this project has been stuck behind the security review, so I mostly want to understand where that stands.

transcript.speaker: Nadia Kaur
transcript.text: Fair. It's taken longer than any of us wanted — the questionnaire touched teams that don't usually review vendors together, and anything touching patient data gets extra scrutiny.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Understood. Is there anything outstanding on our side? More documentation, a call with your reviewers?

transcript.speaker: Nadia Kaur
transcript.text: No, your responses were complete, including the HIPAA and data-handling sections. The remaining answers are drafted internally and I'm waiting on one approval from our platform lead. I expect to close the review out early next week.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: That's genuinely good news. Oliver, once that lands, what's the path to getting us connected?

transcript.speaker: Oliver Hartley
transcript.text: The moment Nadia signs off, I'll provision the Snowflake service account — read-only on the ANALYTICS schema, exactly as specced. It's a same-day job once the review closes, so I won't put a separate date on it.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: And just to confirm scope while we're all here: read-only, ANALYTICS schema only, no raw layer?

transcript.speaker: Oliver Hartley
transcript.text: Correct. Our data governance policy won't allow raw-layer access for external tools — that's where the identifiable lab results live — and honestly you don't need it.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Agreed, we don't. Once the service account exists we can connect the dbt repo the same day, so the chain unblocks quickly.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Hartley
transcript.text: That's what I'm hoping. We've lost about three weeks; if the connection happens next week we can claw most of that back.

transcript.speaker: Nadia Kaur
transcript.text: From my side, no further reviews needed after this one. The tool itself was approved — it was the data-sharing terms for the health data that took time.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Good to know. I won't pile more actions on — the sign-off and the service account are the whole critical path. Anything you need from me?

transcript.speaker: Oliver Hartley
transcript.text: Nothing right now. If provisioning throws anything weird I'll ping you on Slack.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Perfect. Let's speak once the account is live. Thanks both.

meeting.title: Weekly sync
meeting.summary: Weekly implementation sync. Warehouse connection is healthy after last week's credential rotation. The customer will finish tagging the exposure models by Thursday, and the vendor side will share a draft of the executive dashboard before the next call.
action_items: Finish tagging the exposure models by Thursday
Share a draft of the executive dashboard before the next call
key_decisions: Executive dashboard will use weekly grain, not daily
meeting.notes: Credential rotation last week caused a brief sync failure; resolved same day. No open incidents.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Morning both. Usual run-through: connection status, then the exposure work, then the exec dashboard.

transcript.speaker: Speaker 1
transcript.text: Connection's been solid since the credential rotation. The overnight syncs have all gone green.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Good — that outage last Tuesday was the rotation, nothing structural. Okay, exposures. Where did the tagging land?

transcript.speaker: Speaker 1
transcript.text: About two thirds done. The finance models are tagged, the ops ones aren't yet. I'll finish tagging the exposure models by Thursday.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Thursday works. Once they're tagged the lineage view fills itself in, which the exec audience will love.

transcript.speaker: Speaker 2
transcript.text: On that — leadership asked what the exec dashboard will actually look like. Do we have anything to show them?

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Not yet, but I can fix that. I'll share a draft of the executive dashboard before our next call so you have something concrete to circulate.

transcript.speaker: Speaker 2
transcript.text: That would help a lot. One design question: daily or weekly numbers? Daily felt noisy in the old tool.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: For an exec audience, weekly. Daily grain invites questions about single bad days that don't mean anything.

transcript.speaker: Speaker 2
transcript.text: Agreed, let's commit to weekly grain for that one.

transcript.speaker: Speaker 1
transcript.text: Fine by me. Anything you need from us for the draft?

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: No, I have enough from discovery. Alright — tagging by Thursday, draft dashboard from me before next week. Short and sweet today.

transcript.speaker: Speaker 1
transcript.text: Perfect, thanks. Speak next week.

meeting.title: Quick catch-up
action_items: Send the SSO troubleshooting guide today
meeting.notes: Ad-hoc call, no calendar invite. Two analysts hit a redirect error when signing in via SSO this morning.

transcript.speaker: Speaker 1
transcript.text: Thanks for jumping on quickly. Two of our analysts got a redirect error signing in this morning.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Both via SSO, or one on password login?

transcript.speaker: Speaker 1
transcript.text: Both SSO. Everyone else got in fine, which is the confusing part.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: That usually means those two are missing the app assignment in your identity provider rather than anything on our side.

transcript.speaker: Speaker 1
transcript.text: Ah — they did both join the data team this month. That would fit.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Almost certainly it. I'll send you our SSO troubleshooting guide today — page two shows exactly where the assignment lives.

transcript.speaker: Speaker 1
transcript.text: Great, I'll forward it to IT. Second thing, very quick: the training session next month, can we bring a few extra people?

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: How many are we talking?

transcript.speaker: Speaker 1
transcript.text: Maybe four or five from the ops side. Nothing confirmed yet, they're still deciding.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: That's fine capacity-wise. Let me know once they decide and we'll size the workshop accordingly.

transcript.speaker: Speaker 1
transcript.text: Will do. That was everything — appreciate the fast turnaround.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: No problem, guide is on its way today.

meeting.title: Flock Freight status call
meeting.summary: Short, noncommittal status call with Flock Freight. Derek acknowledged the open items are stalled on his side but would not commit to dates — internal quarter-end reporting is consuming the team. Maya offered help; Derek deferred everything to 'after quarter-end' without specifics. No new work agreed.
meeting.notes: Derek joined 5 minutes late and dropped early for another call. Engagement noticeably lower than in May.

transcript.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
transcript.text: Hi Derek — thanks for squeezing this in, I know things are hectic. I wanted to check where the open items stand on your side.

transcript.speaker: Derek Liang
transcript.text: Yeah, sorry for being slow lately. Honestly, nothing has moved. Quarter-end reporting has eaten the whole team.

transcript.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
transcript.text: Understood. Is there a point in the next couple of weeks where the warehouse permissions work could realistically restart?

transcript.speaker: Derek Liang
transcript.text: Hard to say. Maybe after quarter-end? I'd need to check with our platform person and she's buried too.

transcript.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
transcript.text: Okay. Would it help if we took more of it — for instance we could draft the permission grants so it's a review rather than a build?

transcript.speaker: Derek Liang
transcript.text: Possibly. Let me think about it — I don't want to promise review time I don't have either.

transcript.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
transcript.text: That's fair. And the pilot-group question from May — any movement on who'd be in it?

transcript.speaker: Derek Liang
transcript.text: Not yet. We should probably revisit that once reporting season is over. I just can't put a date on it right now.

transcript.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
transcript.text: Alright. I don't want to pile pressure on a crunch — I'd rather find the realistic restart point than invent deadlines we'll miss.

transcript.speaker: Derek Liang
transcript.text: Appreciate that. Truthfully, mid-July is my best guess for when we can breathe again, but don't hold me to it.

transcript.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
transcript.text: Noted as a guess, not a promise. I'll keep our side warm so nothing rots in the meantime.

transcript.speaker: Derek Liang
transcript.text: Thanks Maya. Sorry — I have to drop for another call. Talk soon.

transcript.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
transcript.text: No problem, go. Talk soon.

meeting.title: Function Health weekly sync
meeting.summary: Weekly sync with Function Health. Infosec questionnaire finally signed off; Sam to send the static IP allowlist, Oliver to create the Snowflake service account by Friday.
action_items: Sam to send the Quarry static IP list by tomorrow
Oliver to create the Snowflake service account by Friday
key_decisions: Security sign-off unblocks the warehouse connection chain
meeting.notes: Three-week security stall finally resolved. Warehouse connection chain can now move.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Morning both. Nadia, I'm hoping you have news on the security review.

transcript.speaker: Nadia Rahman
transcript.text: I do — good news finally. We signed off the infosec questionnaire yesterday afternoon. That review is done from our side.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Fantastic. That's been the long pole for three weeks, so everything downstream can move now.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Hartley
transcript.text: Which means the service account is on me next. What exactly do you need?

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: A read-only Snowflake service account scoped to the analytics schema — the de-identified marts, not the raw PHI — and our static IPs added to your network policy.

transcript.speaker: Nadia Rahman
transcript.text: The IP allowlist goes through my team — send us the list and we'll process it with the sign-off paperwork.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Will do — I'll send over the Quarry static IP list by tomorrow so your team can add it to the network policy.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Hartley
transcript.text: And I'll get the Snowflake service account created by Friday. Platform team has capacity this week.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Perfect. Once both land, we connect the warehouse and the repo the same day.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Hartley
transcript.text: One thing to flag — our HIPAA audit season starts in August, so we may want to think about access reviews before then.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Noted, let's scope that once we're connected rather than now.

transcript.speaker: Nadia Rahman
transcript.text: Fine by me. It was mostly a heads-up.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Great. So: questionnaire is done, IP list from me tomorrow, service account from Oliver by Friday. Real progress.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Hartley
transcript.text: Feels good to be moving again. Thanks Sam.
